To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have discovered a panel of human anti-CA IX scFv antibodies, that specifically recognize and bind to CA IX, and are capable of inhibiting the CA IX carbonic anhydrases activity, a unique feature of these antibodies.
a new panel of human anti-CA IX antibodies was discovered by phage display technology and these antibodies have unique biological properties.

(i) human anti-CA9 antibodies were discovered by using phage-display technology; (ii) these antibodies are diverse in their binding affinities and biological properties, including the inhibition of CAIX catalytic activity, a unique feature of these anti-CAIX scFv antibodies; (iii) the CAIX epitopes were mapped and the antibodies were epitope-mapped to the CA domain of CAIX.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel human anti-CA IX antibodies and characterization of their unique biological activities.
the discovery, development, and application of new anti-cancer agents.
the development of novel diagnostic tools and immunotherapies for RCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of paramagnetic proteolipsomal particles for antibody selections from large human antibody libraries is a novel, efficient and effective method to obtain human antibodies with unique properties.
this work is a proof-of-principle study for a novel approach for development of anti-CAIX therapeutic and diagnostic agents.
we have developed a novel method for selection and characterization of a panel of human anti-CA IX antibodies, which have a unique set of biological properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a panel of unique human antibodies that recognize the CAIX protein, some of which are capable of inducing CAIX internalization and inhibiting its enzymatic activity.
we have developed a novel technology to select human anti-CA9 antibodies that can be used in a variety of applications including diagnostics and therapeutics.

the human anti-CA IX antibodies discovered through phage-display technology have unique properties that may have important implications in development of novel immunotherapeutics for the treatment of RCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CA domain is an important target for development of new diagnostic tools and immunotherapeutics for RCC treatment, and that human antibodies are better than murine mAbs for this purpose.

phage display technology is a powerful tool for the discovery of novel human antibodies against tumor antigens and that the use of proteoliposomes for antibody selection may be an effective approach for identifying antibodies with unique biological properties.
phage-display technology is an efficient tool for discovery of new anti-CAIX human antibodies and that the CA domain of CAIX may be targeted for development of new anti-CCIX antibodies.
